minutes.headline: School Committee approved the FY20 school budget by roll call, reluctantly, and cut math graduation requirement to three credits.
minutes.summary: The committee approved a line-item transfer, minutes, donations, a change to high school math graduation requirements, and extended day program changes. After the superintendent reported on talks with the town manager, members voted by roll call to approve the FY20 budget, several saying they were unhappy with the bottom line. They also signed a Fund Our Future resolution and heard a facilities update and a student council trip report.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the FY20 school budget at the stated bottom line by roll call, with members saying they would vote yes.
The committee accepted a change setting the high school math graduation requirement at three credits, after a long discussion.
The committee approved extended day changes, including block pricing; staff are to draft a parent communication and return with a revised handbook.
The committee approved a line item transfer so the water consumption line has enough funds for FY19, with the electricity line covering it.
The superintendent is to analyze fundraising with school leadership and return with a recommendation on criteria and guidelines.

why_it_matters: The FY20 school budget vote sets the school share of the spending that goes to Town Meeting and, in turn, to the tax bill.
The math requirement change affects what current and future high school students must take to graduate, and the extended day changes affect what families pay for before- and after-school care.
watch_next: The revised extended day handbook, which staff are to bring back to the committee.
The superintendent's recommendation on fundraising criteria and guidelines.
